denominator: distinct session_id with an accepted session.end or session.error row
population: accepted activity rows (after dedup and rejects). Every terminal session has an accepted session.start because orphans are rejected. Sessions with no terminal row are excluded.
late_policy: late rows are accepted and only flagged (the batch has no watermark), so a late terminal row still makes its session terminal
null_policy: none possible: event_type, session_id and event_time are required fields, and rows missing them are rejected

population: duration = terminal event_time_utc - session.start event_time_utc; pandas Series.quantile with linear interpolation between closest ranks
late_policy: included. Lateness concerns ingest_time, and the duration uses event_time only
null_policy: a session without an accepted start would have no duration and be excluded; the curated data has none. latency_ms is never used as the duration, only as a cross-check (disagreement > 1 s reported)

population: complete = at least one accepted llm.turn, and the accepted sequence_numbers are exactly 1..max (no gap, no repeat). A row rejected for any reason except DUPLICATE_EVENT_ID (which leaves one accepted copy) leaves a gap, so the session counts as incomplete.
late_policy: late rows are accepted, so they fill their sequence slot
null_policy: sequence_number is required; rows without it are rejected, which leaves a gap

population: covered = the alert is linked to exactly one session at N = 60 s: matched (one candidate flow) plus ambiguous alerts whose candidate flows all belong to one session. Ambiguous alerts spanning several sessions, and unmatched alerts, are not covered. Strict (matched only) and on-platform variants are reported next to it.
late_policy: not applicable: alerts and flows carry no ingest_time; |delta t| <= N is the only time rule
null_policy: an alert without a session is not covered; it is never force-matched

denominator: received records per source = accepted + rejected (every received record lands in exactly one of the two; the pipeline asserts this)
population: the four event sources. Headline = agent_activity.parquet; the overall rate is pooled over all four. Reference files are cleaned by dedup and repair, not rejected, so they are not counted.
late_policy: late rows are not rejected in batch (no LATE_BEYOND_WATERMARK), so lateness does not raise this rate
null_policy: a null in a required field is a reject (MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD) and is counted

population: late = ingest_time_utc - event_time_utc > 10 s. Only agent_activity has an ingest_time, so the other sources have no lateness. Late duplicate copies were already removed by dedup (the earliest ingest is kept) and are not counted.
late_policy: this metric is the late policy's measurement: late rows are kept and flagged LATE
null_policy: none possible: both timestamps are required and a malformed one is a reject
null-excluded: the count stays null, cost_usd is null and both are left out of sums and averages, never imputed as 0 (effect shown by missing_token_effect)
